consequence.statement: Existing policies keep nested variable substitution unless they adopt the new notation; using `{{- ... }}` limits substitution to one pass so Kyverno does not attempt to resolve `{{ }}` content inside the substituted data (e.g. an HCL string from a ConfigMap).
consequence.remediation: Where substituted rule data contains `{{ }}` that Kyverno must not resolve, use the `{{- ... }}` declaration (e.g. `{{- hcl }}`) for shallow substitution.

original.statement: Kyverno 1.13.0 adds a `{{- ... }}` notation for shallow (one-time) variable substitution, letting a policy substitute rule data (e.g. an HCL string defined in a ConfigMap) without Kyverno attempting to resolve the nested `{{ }}` variables inside it.

decision.reason: [ev-cc61618a6c99] lists this under "Other Features and Enhancements". It says Kyverno performs nested variable substitution by default, and that the new `{{- ... }}` notation is an opt-in way to substitute only once. Nothing in the excerpt says existing policies fail, are rejected or behave differently if the operator does nothing, so "none" (informational) with low severity is supported. The CRD diffs (e.g. [ev-9348cb2d7f00]) cover the unrelated apiCall.default field and do not bear on this consequence.
